newsitem.title: USA: Calif '96 disaster losses tame at $119 mln so far.
newsitem.headline: Calif '96 disaster losses tame at $119 mln so far.

text.p: California suffered losses estimated at more than $119 million in 1996 from major fire and flood emergencies, the governor's office of emergency services said on Tuesday.

Gov. Pete Wilson proclaimed states of emergency in 13 California counties for flood and fire emergencies. These 1996 figures did not include damage from the current storms sweeping the Northwest, the office of emergency services said.

Disaster damage losses for 1996 were low compared to previous years. The loss figure so far was the lowest since 1988, and for the first time in six years, the state's losses did not exceed $1 billion, the state said.
The California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection responded to 7,961 fires which burned 232,541 acres, nearly twice the 124,191 acres burned in 1995.

The only major disaster in 1996 that required federal assistance was a series of October fires in Los Angeles, San Diego, Ventura and Orange counties. President Clinton issued an emergency declaration allowing those counties to recover 75 percent of some emergency response costs.
